column2: What desire shall I give you today? Say what you wish, child. With joined palms he said: "Let my devotion to you be firm."
Having so given the boon, the god, saluted by the divine sages and praised by the gods, vanished right there.
When the blessed one with his followers had vanished, lord of the Yadavas, the sage came to the hermitage and told me this here.
Hear, best of men, for success, the names that Tandi told me, famed from the beginning.
The grandfather spoke ten thousand names of Sharva in the Vedas, and likewise a thousand in the scriptures.
These secret names of the blessed one, Achyuta, Tandi told long ago to the great soul by the god's grace, lord of gods.
[Upamanyu said:] "I shall praise Sthanu with names spoken by Brahma, spoken by sages, born of the Vedas and Vedangas, famed in all worlds,
true, made by the great, perfected, accomplishing all aims, made with devotion by the sage Tandi, whose self was made by the god,
as told, world-famous, by sages who see the truth: the best, first, leading to heaven, good for all beings, auspicious, heard everywhere in the world, brought down from Brahma's world.
That secret, supreme, eternal Brahman that was told: I shall tell it, best of the Yadava family; listen attentively to me.
As you are a devotee of the Supreme Lord Bhava, the highest, I shall make you hear that eternal Brahman.
It cannot be told in full in detail by anyone about Sharva, even if joined with hundreds of years, of his glories.
Whose beginning, middle and end are not reached even by the gods: who could tell his qualities in full, Madhava?
But I shall tell the deeds of the great god in brief words and syllables, as I can and by his grace.
Of the beginningless and endless great soul, the womb of all, of the unmanifest source, I shall tell a certain summary of names.
Hear the summary of names of the wise one of universal form, giver of boons, the choicest, as told by the lotus-born.
Ten thousand names that the great-grandfather spoke, I have churned them in mind and drawn them out like ghee from curds.
As the essence of a mountain, as honey is the essence of a flower of gold, as cream is the essence of ghee, so is this essence drawn out.
This removes all sin and is joined with the four Vedas; it should be learned with effort and borne by the pure of mind, a great peace-giving, nourishing, rakshasa-destroying purifier.
This should be given to a devotee, a faithful believer, and not to one of unbelieving form, an unbeliever of unmastered self.
He who envies the god, the self of beings, the Pinaka-bearer, goes to hell, Krishna, with his ancestors and followers.

This is meditation, this is yoga, this is the unsurpassed object of meditation, this is to be muttered, this is knowledge, this is the supreme secret; knowing it even at the end of life, one would go to the highest goal.
Pure, auspicious, holy, benefiting, this best; I shall recite, mighty-armed, the best of hymns.
Brahma, grandfather of all worlds, long ago made this and appointed it king of all divine hymns.
From then this is famed as the king of hymns of the great lord, worshipped by the immortals in the world; and this king of hymns was brought down from Brahma's world.
Because Tandi told it long ago, it became known as made by Tandi; and it was brought down from heaven to the earth by Tandi.
Auspicious of all auspiciousness, destroying all sin, I shall recite, mighty-armed, the best of hymns.
What is the Brahman of brahmans, the highest of breaths, the splendour of splendours, the austerity of austerities,
the peace of peaces, the radiance of radiances, the self-controlled of the self-controlled, the wisdom of the wise,
the god of gods, the sage of sages, the sacrifice of sacrifices, the auspicious of the auspicious,
the Rudra of Rudras, the lord of lords, the yogi of yogis, the cause of causes,
from whom the worlds arise and into whom they do not again arise, the self of all beings, Hara of boundless splendour.
Hear the thousand and eight names of Sharva, hearing which, best of men, you will gain all desires.

Whom Brahma and the other gods do not know, nor the great sages: who will praise that lord of the world who is to be praised, worshipped and saluted?
Putting devotion first, I praised the lord of sacrifice, Vasu; then, having obtained leave, the best of the wise praised him.
Praising the auspicious god with these names that increase nourishment, constantly joined and pure, one gains the self by the self.
This is the highest Brahman, sung by the Self-born himself; sages and gods praise the supreme with this.
Praised, Mahadeva is pleased with the names of the self; the blessed one, tender to devotees, establishes them in himself.
So too among men those men who are chiefly believers, faithful, in many births, by hymns,
waking and sleeping, going and standing on the road, praise, and being praised are pleased and delight, through ten million births in the many wombs of rebirth.
For the creature whose sin is purified, devotion to Bhava is born; and the devotion born in Bhava is exclusive and in every way.
The cause fostered in him, freed from everything on every side: this is hard to get among gods and is not gained among men.
Unobstructed, firm, unwavering devotion to Rudra arises in men by his grace alone, by which, their minds gone to that state, they reach supreme success.
Those men who go to him in every way, thinking of him as supreme, the god, tender to those who take refuge, raises them out of rebirth.
Other gods do not so liberate men from rebirth, other than Mahadeva, even by the power of austerity.
Thus, Krishna, the blessed lord of being and non-being, clothed in a hide, was praised by Tandi of pure understanding, a match for Indra.
Brahma himself bore this hymn of the blessed one; Brahma told it to Shakra, Shakra told it to Death.
Death told it to the Rudras; from the Rudras it came to Tandi, gained by great austerity by Tandi in Brahma's abode.
Tandi told it to Shukra and Gautama; Bhargava told it, and Gautama told it to Vaivasvata Manu, Madhava.
To Narayana the Sadhya, Manu told it, to the wise beloved one; the blessed Sadhya Narayana Achyuta told it to Yama.
The blessed Vaivasvata Yama told it to Nachiketas, and Nachiketas told it to Markandeya, Varshneya.
From Markandeya I received it by observance, Janardana; and to you too, slayer of foes, I give this famed hymn today, leading to heaven, giving health, long life, fortune and strength.
Danavas, yakshas, rakshasas, pishachas, yatudhanas, guhyakas and serpents do not obstruct him.
He who recites it, pure, a student of Brahman, master of his senses, with unbroken yoga for a year, would gain the fruit of the horse sacrifice.

Long ago, son, as I practised supreme austerity on Meru for a son, this hymn was recited, great king.
mahabharata:13:18.3	I gained those desires, son of Pandu; and you too will gain all desires from Sharva.
Then Chaturshirsha, the dear friend of Shakra, famed as Alambayana, merciful, said:

Having reached Gokarna and practised austerity for a hundred years, a hundred sons were obtained from Sharva, son of the king Pandu, long ago,
mahabharata:13:18.6	not born of a womb, self-controlled, knowers of dharma, of fine splendour, ageless, sorrowless, living a hundred thousand years.
And the blessed Valmiki also said to Yudhishthira: "In a dispute over the Saman, sages said to me, 'You are a brahmana-killer', and I was in that moment seized by that unrighteousness, Bharata.
Taking refuge, I praised the sinless Ishana, and was freed helplessly from sin; then the destroyer of sorrow, slayer of Tripura, said to me, 'Your fame will be foremost.'"
And Jamadagnya, best of upholders of dharma, said to Kaunteya, seated among the sages, dear one, glowing like fire:
The blessed one with Shiva's form, Shikhandin, said this to me, and all I got was by the grace of that wise one.
Asita and Devala said to the king, Pandu's son: "By Shakra's curse, Kaunteya, my dharma was heaped, destroyed; Bhava gave me that dharma and foremost fame and long life."
The sage Gritsamada, dear friend of Shakra, the blessed one, bright as Brihaspati, said to Ajamidha:

The blessed Vasishtha, son of Manu Chakshusha, said in the thousand-year sacrifice of the inconceivable Shatakratu, when the Saman was uttered by me:
mahabharata:13:18.17	'The Rathantara, best of the twice-born, is not right; reconsider with understanding, leaving joy, best of the twice-born. You, evil-minded, have done a sin that carries sacrifice away.'
mahabharata:13:18.18	Having so spoken in great anger, he said again, enraged: 'Devoid of wisdom, sorrowful, always fearful, a forest-dweller for ten thousand and eighteen hundred years,
mahabharata:13:18.19	in a country where water and grass are lost, free of deer and others, with trees unfit for sacrifice, frequented by ruru deer and lions, you will be a cruel deer, joined with great sorrow.'
mahabharata:13:18.20	At the end of his speech, Partha, I became a deer; then, when I had taken refuge, the yogi Maheshvara said to me:
mahabharata:13:18.21	'You will be ageless and deathless, free of sorrow; equality, let there be sameness and happiness for you; and may the sacrifice of you two increase.'
mahabharata:13:18.22	Thus the blessed all-pervading one does favours; he is the highest, creator and ordainer, and pleasure and pain always.
mahabharata:13:18.23	This blessed one is inconceivable by deed, mind and speech; dear one, best in battle, no learned man is equal to me in knowledge.
[Jaigishavya said:] "The eightfold lordship was given to me by the blessed one long ago, with little effort, mighty one, at Varanasi, Yudhishthira."
[Gargya said:] "He gave me the wonderful sixty-four-part knowledge of time, pleased, on the bank of the Sarasvati, by mental sacrifice, Pandava.
And a thousand sons equal to me, speakers of Brahman, and life of a hundred thousand years for me with my sons."

[Parashara said:] "Having pleased Sharva long ago, I thought in mind, king: the great ascetic, of great splendour, great yogi, of great fame, Veda Vyasa, abode of prosperity, friend of brahmanas, merciful.
'May I have a son from Maheshvara, as I wish': thinking so in his heart, the best of gods said to me what was in my mind:
'From me, Krishna will be born from the fruit of that; in the creation of Manu Savarni he will also be one of the seven sages.'"
Royal sage, you are not very glad; is it well with you, sinless one? Where have you gone, and whence have you come into a house of displeasure?
The mighty-armed son of Dharma embraced his father and, letting fall tears born of grief, spoke again.
Those gods, O king, welcomed him, the best of sages worshipped the lord with words, the gandharvas attended him praising, and Purahuta gladly welcomed him.
There he saw Govinda, joined with a Brahmic body, indicated by that same likeness as formerly seen.
